sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. Circulation draft, May 2012, 369 pp. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: Sec. 3.6.5 'Bauchi [=Baushi] cluster' (pp. 19-20) gives names, subgroups and wordlist history only; the phonology heading 4.6.1 'Baushi' is empty in this draft; the word 'stress' does not occur in the document.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2011. 'The Shiroro languages' web page, rogerblench.info (Kainji/Shiroro/ShiOP.htm), Internet Archive copy 2015-04-20, plus the Internet Archive's index listing of the whole Kainji folder.
sources.note: Names/classification only; CDX shows the Shiroro folder never held any Baushi wordlist or phonology file, so the 'Blench Baushi wordlist manuscripts' named by the earlier scan were never posted online.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2022. Change Request 2022-022: split of Bauchi [bsf] (rejected 2023-01-20), with new-code request forms for Guda-Wayam, Bandeke, Rubu, Supana, Asamburu; submitted by Iris Sacson, SIL Nigeria.
sources.note: Lexicostatistics and ethnolinguistic identity only; no phonology.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Fittokka Gobak, Benard Abraham, Christina Riepe, Andrew Lewinan & Luther Hon. 2021. Preliminary findings from a sociolinguistic survey of the Bauchi [bsf] - Fungwa [ula] language cluster of Niger State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-062. Dallas: SIL International. 58 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 9.3 'Bauchi-Fungwa phonology' (pp. 16-19) gives consonant and vowel inventories and, under 9.3.3 'prosodic features', only prenasalization, palatalization, labialization and word-final vowel devoicing; Appendix B (p. 36, p. 42) states 'The transcriptions are preliminary since no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features was conducted.' The 200-item wordlists for six Bauchi varieties are tone-marked phonetic transcriptions; no statement on stress/accent or on the tone system.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, edition IV. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: Entries 322 Mɨn (Bauchi Guda), 175 Hɨpɨna, 332 Ndəkə, 400 Rubu, 407 Samburu, 478 Wãyã list only 'Source(s) Blench (2010)/Gimba (2010)/McGill (2012)'; no grammar or phonology references; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Nominal affixing in the Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. In John R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs, 59-106. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Sec. 3.7 The Shiroro languages, p. 94: apart from Rin, 'For the other languages [incl. Baushi] there is only wordlist data.' Nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart & Roger Blench. 2012. Documentation, development, and ideology in the northwestern Kainji languages. In Stuart McGill & Peter K. Austin (eds), Language Documentation and Description 11, 90-135. London: SOAS. doi:10.25894/LDD180
sources.note: Nothing on Baushi stress or tone; table p. 100 lists for Timun (Bauchi-Nguda)/Tiwãyã only 'BA thesis (Gimba 2011), unpublished wordlists (Gimba fieldnotes, KJ700)'; p. 104 mentions the interdental approximants of Nguda/Timun (Harley 2012).
